summary.en: Implement stable value equality, matching hash codes and useful object descriptions.
summary.bn: মান অনুযায়ী equals, মিল থাকা hashCode এবং অর্থপূর্ণ toString লেখো।

notes: The instanceof pattern in equals needs Java 16 or later and runs on Java 17.

sections.title: Give objects a meaningful value contract
Check the contracts on independent objects
Avoid surprising equality across a hierarchy
Describe objects without confusing text with identity
Check both halves of value equality

examples.title: Equal values can have distinct identities
examples.explanationHtml: Two new objects have different identities but equal course codes. println calls the descriptive toString() override.

examples.title: Equal objects must have equal hashes
examples.explanationHtml: Equal course codes produce matching hashes. null and a String are not Course values.

examples.title: Runtime class is not the declared view
examples.explanationHtml: getClass() reports the exact runtime class. instanceof also accepts supertypes such as Object.

examples.title: A hash collision is not equality
examples.explanationHtml: These two fixed String values have equal hash codes but different contents. A hash is a bucket hint rather than a unique identifier.

practice.title: Compare course values
practice.statementHtml: Read two nonempty whitespace-free course codes, each at most 12 ASCII characters. Use immutable Course values. Print equals result and hash-equality result on separate lines.

practice.title: Count equal seats
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..20), a target row and column (1..50), then n row-column pairs in the same range. A final Seat value compares both coordinates and hashes both. Print how many seats equal the target.
hints: Both identity fields must participate in equality.

practice.title: Repair an equals overload
practice.statementHtml: A class declares boolean equals(Course other), but not equals(Object). Explain the consequence through Object references.
practice.answerHtml: equals(Course) overloads rather than overrides Object.equals(Object). An Object reference selects the inherited identity comparison. Declare public boolean equals(Object other), annotate @Override, test type compatibility, and compare the chosen value fields. Override hashCode using those same fields.
hints: Compare the parameter type with the Object API.

practice.title: Protect a hash key
practice.statementHtml: A mutable Course code changes after insertion in a hash-based set. Explain why lookup can fail and suggest a design.
practice.answerHtml: The original hash chose an insertion bucket. Changing equality fields may produce a new hash and send later lookup to another bucket. Use immutable equality fields or remove the key before changing it and reinsert afterward. Stable immutable values are easier to share safely.
hints: A hash container relies on stable key equality.

quiz.prompt: Do equal course values share identity?
quiz.explanation: new allocates different objects; equals compares their code strings.

quiz.prompt: Does a hash collision make these courses equal?
quiz.explanation: String hash collisions are possible and do not imply equal content.

quiz.prompt: Which exact class does getClass() observe through Object?
quiz.explanation: getClass reports the actual Child class, not all its supertypes.

quiz.prompt: Which implication must a correct equals/hashCode pair obey?
quiz.explanation: Hash collisions are allowed; equality without matching hashes violates the contract.

quiz.prompt: What does Object.equals do by default?
quiz.explanation: Value classes must override the default identity-based behaviour when value equality is intended.

quiz.prompt: Which equals requirement describes a.equals(b) matching b.equals(a)?
quiz.explanation: Symmetry requires both directions to agree.
The equals contract rejects null without treating it as an equal value.

quiz.prompt: Why make the demonstrated value class final?
quiz.explanation: Closing the hierarchy makes value equality policy easier to keep symmetric.
options: To avoid subclasses adding incompatible equality state

quiz.prompt: What should a diagnostic toString avoid promising?
quiz.explanation: Debug descriptions can evolve and should not silently become a persistence protocol.
options: A stable serialization format unless documented

quiz.prompt: Which equals signature actually overrides Object?
quiz.explanation: The Object parameter and public access are required; @Override exposes signature mistakes.

keyPoints.en: Object supplies identity equality unless a class overrides it.
keyPoints.bn: ক্লাস ওভাররাইড না করলে Object পরিচয় অনুযায়ী সমতা যাচাই করে।

keyPoints.en: Value equality must be reflexive, symmetric and transitive.
keyPoints.bn: মানভিত্তিক সমতা নিজের সঙ্গে সত্য, দুই দিকেই সমান এবং ট্রানজিটিভ হতে হয়।

keyPoints.en: Equal values require matching hash codes.
keyPoints.bn: সমান মানের অবজেক্টের hashCode একই হতে হয়।

keyPoints.en: Hash collisions do not establish equality.
keyPoints.bn: hashCode মিলে গেলেই অবজেক্ট সমান হয় না।

keyPoints.en: getClass returns the exact runtime class.

examQuestions.question: State the equals contract and the hashCode implication.
examQuestions.answerHtml: equals must be reflexive, symmetric, transitive and consistent while relevant state stays unchanged. A non-null value is unequal to null. Equal objects must have equal hashes. Unequal values may collide, and hashes need not remain identical across separate program executions.

examQuestions.question: Explain why inheritance can make value equality asymmetric.
examQuestions.answerHtml: A base point may compare only coordinates while a coloured subclass requires coordinates and colour. The base could accept the child while the child rejects the base. Close the value class, use composition, or define a carefully shared hierarchy-wide equality policy.

examQuestions.question: Design equality for an immutable seat identified by row and column.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Make Seat final and store two private final ints. equals(Object) checks identity, type, then both coordinates. hashCode combines both fields, for example 31 * row + column. toString can display both coordinates without affecting equality.
